note_tweet.text:
Running a 145B-scale model traditionally involved multi-GPU server setups, often with H100s or H200s.

Edge0-145B takes a different approach: a single 16–24GB consumer GPU, 32–64GB system RAM, and SSD offloading.

The trade-off is throughput and concurrency. It's not a replacement for a multi-GPU server, but it makes local inference possible with much less hardware.

note_tweet.text:
35B parameters on a phone. Sounds like a lot to squeeze into RAM.

Here's the thing: not all the experts need to be in memory at the same time.

With Edge0-35B, we keep expert weights in local storage and bring in the ones needed for inference.

We also use a trained prerouter to predict which experts are needed next, so we can start loading them while the model is still working on the current token.

Still a 35B model. Just a smarter way to handle its memory.

note_tweet.text:
A robot doesn't need to write a 2,000-word essay while avoiding a chair.

Smart glasses don't need to run a massive model just to understand “turn up the volume.”

And your phone doesn't need a cloud-sized setup for every AI task.

We talk a lot about how big a model can run on a device.

Maybe we should talk more about what that device actually needs the model to do.
